notes.title: Major Update – “The Harbor”
notes.notes:
Welcome to one of the biggest updates yet! Reworked, reloaded, and refined the experience – and now it's time for you to dive into the fog.




[hr][/hr]
New Map: “The Habor”


Say hello to The Habor, a gritty, fog-drenched harbor where danger hides behind every container.
There are no weapons at spawn – you’ll need to explore, scavenge, and secure your gear before the chaos starts.
The low visibility makes this a tense, tactical experience. Who’s breathing behind that crate? Friend or foe? You’ll have to find out the hard way.


[hr][/hr]
Performance Upgrades


Cleaned up, tightened code, and squeezed out unnecessary overhead to give you a smoother ride across all machines.

Faster loading times – spend more time playing, less time watching loading bars.

Reduced VRAM usage – your GPU will thank you, especially on longer sessions.

FSR updated – now supports a wider range of graphics cards and brings real FPS gains, not just better anti-aliasing.

More FPS - shooting smoother with +-50% more Real*FPS 

*without DLSS or FSR 


[hr][/hr]
Gameplay & Bugfixes

Fixed the infamous pistol reload bug. No more empty click-clicks in the heat of battle.

Optimized player spawn zones.

General polish and tweaks across lighting, fog rendering, and map memory usage.


[hr][/hr]
Looking Ahead…


The fog hasn’t even cleared yet, and already working on the next big thing.

Coming up in the next major update:

A brand-new map is in the works – fresh terrain, fresh chaos.

GUI improvements to make your interactions smoother.

Networking optimizations to make multiplayer more stable, snappier, and rage-quit resistant.

Plus: a handful of smaller tweaks, fixes, and polish to keep everything feeling crisp.


[hr][/hr]


Final Notes
As always: new content means new unknowns. If you find bugs, please report them — preferably before they start a rebellion.




The fog is thick, the docks are dangerous, and your enemies are lurking. Good luck out there.

notes.title: Patch Notes – Update #1
notes.notes:
Fixes & Tweaks:

Fixed an issue where players could shoot through some walls.

Fixed a bug where players became invincible after finishing a round while morphed. Sorry, you’re mortal again.

Fixed some crashes related to FSR. If it’s still crashing your game, please let me know.

Fixed a crash that occurred when multiple cameras were active at the same time.

Fixed a raytracing Luma glitch that made things... glow wrong.

Fixed a missing collider on the parking garage map.

Fixed several LOD settings that caused objects to pop in too late.
[hr][/hr]


Gameplay & Tech:

Adjusted the range of all weapons. Think it’s too much or too little? Please cry at the steam forum.

Upgraded the game to Unity 6.1.7 for better stability and future features.

Added a few logs and debug tools to keep an eye on things behind the curtain.

Prepped the world and scripts for the upcoming maps and features. The future is coming...
[hr][/hr]


Reminder:
Fixes can sometimes create new bugs. If you notice anything weird — crashes, glitches, or suspiciously sentient morphs — let me know!
[hr][/hr]


What’s next?
The next big update will include:

A brand-new map

GPU and VRAM optimizations

After that, FSR should bring better FPS on a wider range of GPUs – not just act as fancy anti-aliasing.

And, of course, more improvements



Thanks for playing, testing, breaking things, and reporting back — you're helping shape this game every step of the way!

notes.title: The Early Access Release Date Is Set!
notes.notes:
Yes, it’s happening. We finally have a date for the Early Access launch of Morphing Bullets!

Development has been progressing faster than expected. The final tests are underway, the last bugs are being squashed, and things are looking really solid.
In fact, a few features that originally planned after the Early Access launch are already finished... and might sneak their way in earlier than planned.

Still taking a few more weeks to fine-tune everything – not because we’re behind, but because we don’t want to rush the final details. This also gives us time to ensure stability, polish, and maybe a little surprise here and there.


 Save the Date:
